Answer: B
Reason: The axial CT image (Figure 2b) demonstrates dense calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), which is a characteristic chronic vascular change in Takayasu arteritis. This finding correlates with the chest X-ray showing a smaller, hyperlucent right hemithorax due to longstanding oligemia, rather than an acute embolic event or primary left-sided pathology.
